source: NCERT Class XI, An Introduction to Indian Art (Part 1), Ch. 3 (Arts of the Mauryan Period).

sections.heading: 1. Mauryan Art — Context
points: The **Mauryan period** (c. 322–185 BCE), especially under **Ashoka**, saw the rise of monumental art linked to the **state** and to **Buddhism**.
Categories: **court art (pillars, palaces)** and **popular art (yakshas, yakshis, pottery, caves)**.
**Megasthenes** (Greek envoy) described the splendour of the Mauryan palace at Pataliputra.

sections.heading: 2. Pillars and Capitals
points: **Ashokan pillars** — tall, monolithic, highly polished **sandstone** columns bearing edicts; famous for the **'Mauryan polish'**.
The **Sarnath Lion Capital** (four lions back to back) is the most famous — India's **National Emblem**; below it the **Dharma Chakra (wheel)** — on the National Flag.
The capitals feature animals (lion, bull, elephant, horse) and the wheel.

sections.heading: 3. Sculpture — Yakshas and Yakshis
points: **Yaksha and Yakshi** figures — large, free-standing stone statues (folk deities); e.g. the **Didarganj Yakshi** (from Patna) — a famous polished sculpture with a chauri (fly-whisk).
These show mastery of stone carving and the popular religious tradition.
Monumental in size and finely finished.

sections.heading: 4. Rock-cut Caves and Stupas
points: **Rock-cut architecture** began — the **Barabar and Nagarjuni caves** (Bihar), dedicated to the **Ajivika sect**; noted for their polished interiors.
**Stupas** — Buddhist relic mounds; the core of the **Sanchi Stupa** was built in the Mauryan period (under Ashoka).
Ashoka is traditionally said to have built many stupas to spread Buddhism.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Sarnath Lion Capital = National Emblem of India; wheel = on National Flag.
Ashokan pillars = polished monolithic sandstone ('Mauryan polish').
Didarganj Yakshi = famous polished Mauryan sculpture (holds a chauri).
Barabar/Nagarjuni caves = earliest rock-cut caves (for the Ajivikas).
Sanchi Stupa core built under Ashoka.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **Sarnath Lion Capital** (four lions) is India's **National Emblem**.
The **Barabar caves** were dedicated to the **Ajivika** sect.
The **Didarganj Yakshi** is a Mauryan polished sculpture.
The high shine on Mauryan sculpture is called the **'Mauryan polish'**.
